rows.explanation: Paul says one trespass brought condemnation to all, matching the ayah’s universal condition of loss, while the verse also answers with justification and life through Christ.
Paul says sin entered the world and death passed to all people because all sinned, describing a universal human ruin.
It says all have sinned and fall short of God’s glory, matching the claim that humanity is in loss.
It says Scripture has confined all under sin, describing a universal human condition of failure.
Jesus says the believer has eternal life, will not come into condemnation, and has passed from death to life.
It says whoever believes in the Son will not perish but have everlasting life.
It says all die in Adam but are made alive in Christ, giving the reverse outcome.
It says all have turned aside and become corrupt, describing humanity’s universal failure.
It says all have gone astray like sheep, using a universal image of being lost.
Jesus says his sheep will never perish and have eternal life.
It says there is no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus.
It says there is no righteous person on earth who always does good and never sins.
It says all are unclean, all fade like a leaf, and their iniquities carry them away, combining universal failure with an image of loss.
It says the whole world is guilty before God, describing humanity’s universal condemnation.
It says God will swallow up death in victory and wipe away tears, reversing the image of humanity’s ruin.
It says no living person can be justified in God’s sight, describing a universal human shortfall.
It says every person, even at their best, is vanity, portraying humanity as futile.
It says “we all” were by nature children of wrath, extending the condition to all people.
It says the whole world lies in wickedness, describing humanity as universally under an evil condition.
It says God made people alive with Christ even when they were dead in sins, reversing death with life.
It says mortality will put on immortality and death will be swallowed up in victory.
It says the way of righteousness leads to life and its path has no death, reversing loss with life.
